title: Phase 1: ANTLR toolchain proving ground
description: Build openCypher tools/grammar Maven module against pinned submodule cypher.xml -> Cypher.g4, commit to marsdb-query/grammar/Cypher.g4. Fetch rrevenantt fork jar, run -Dlanguage=Rust, commit to marsdb-query/src/generated/. Add antlr-rust=0.3.0-beta dep. Prove trivial query parses via scratch test. pest parser untouched.

title: Phase 0: TCK filter + fast feedback loop
description: Add env var/CLI arg to marsdb-tck/src/main.rs restricting walk_feature_files to a category/dir, default unfiltered. Needed before parser rewrite work starts so iteration doesn't require full 3880-scenario runs.

title: Planner start-point selection: pick cheapest pattern endpoint via index/label cardinality instead of written order
description: Design review finding: build_match_plan executes the pattern in written order — MATCH (a:Common)-->(b:Rare {indexed}) scans Common instead of seeking Rare and expanding backwards. Unbounded per-query factor. The O(1) cardinality primitives already exist (index_match_count_in_txn, NODE_LABEL_INDEX multimap len): compare candidate start endpoints, pick cheapest, build the Expand chain from there (reversing hop directions). Most of a cost-based optimizer's practical value at ~1% of its complexity; no stats infrastructure needed.

title: Executor row-slot refactor: replace HashMap<String,Binding> rows with plan-time slot-resolved Vec<Binding>
description: Design review finding: executor.rs:389 BindingRow = HashMap<String,Binding>; Expand clones the whole string-keyed map per emitted neighbor row (executor.rs:~3127). Allocation scales rows*hops*vars. Fix: resolve variable names to slot indices at plan-build time (all names statically known in LogicalPlan), rows become Vec<Binding>. Expected 5-20x on multi-hop MATCH; prerequisite for parallel executor (parallelizing map-cloning just burns cores). Biggest single read-path lever identified in the 2026-08 design review.

title: Cache opened redb table handles per write transaction instead of reopening per *_in_txn call
description:
Found in the design review and confirmed by real flamegraph data (mars-9ja's
re-profile, see its comment): WriteTransaction::open_table sums to 23.67% of
total replay time across ~26 monomorphized call sites, on the real
9,771-statement recommendations bulk load. The single largest identified cost
in that profile -- bigger than create_edge_in_txn (18.05%), index::lookup_exact
(9.96%), or the residual per-statement parse (7.38%).

Every *_in_txn helper in marsdb-graph (create_node_in_txn, create_edge_in_txn,
delete_node_in_txn, set_node_prop_in_txn, index::on_node_created, etc.) does
its own open_table/open_multimap_table fresh, every call -- redb table open
is root lookup + handle setup, small individually but happening constantly
in any bulk-load or multi-write-per-statement inner loop.

Fix direction (from the design review): a statement- or transaction-scoped
struct holding already-opened table handles, threaded through the *_in_txn
call chain instead of each one opening its own. Complicated by redb's
Table<'txn> lifetimes tying a handle to the WriteTransaction's borrow --
that's presumably why it wasn't done already. Needs a real design pass on
how to thread the handle cache through without fighting the borrow checker
(a struct borrowing &WriteTransaction with lazily-populated Option<Table<'_>>
fields per table is one shape; worth checking whether redb offers anything
that makes this cheaper before hand-rolling it).

Verify with the same replay-only flamegraph
(marsdb/examples/convert_only.rs + profile_load.rs, both currently
untracked/scratch -- may be worth committing them as real tooling given
how directly they've paid off across mars-9ja and this issue) -- expect
the open_table percentage to drop close to zero, total replay time to
drop meaningfully below 5.25s.

comments.author: knoguchi
comments.text:
Implementation guidance (from review):

THE GOTCHA: redb write transactions error at runtime (TableAlreadyOpen) on a
second live handle to the same table. So "cache handles" can't be a
transparent memo inside free functions -- it forces the shape: one
statement-scoped context struct *owning* every handle, and every *_in_txn
signature switches from &WriteTransaction to &mut TxnCtx. The current code
dodges TableAlreadyOpen by scoping each open in a block and dropping before
the next -- that's exactly the pattern being deleted.

SHAPE THAT WORKS:

pub struct WriteCtx<'txn> {
    nodes: Table<'txn, u64, &'static [u8]>,
    edges: Table<'txn, u64, &'static [u8]>,
    adj_out: MultimapTable<'txn, u64, &'static [u8]>,
    // ... all 12, opened eagerly in WriteCtx::new(&txn)
}

Eager beats lazy (Option/OnceCell per table): post-#152 every table exists,
opens are cheap *once*, and eager kills the borrow gymnastics of lazily
opening field B while field A is mutably borrowed. Read path gets a sibling
ReadCtx or stays as-is -- the flame says writes are where the 24% lives, so
scope v1 to the write path only, keep Txn-taking read helpers untouched.

COST: mechanical but wide -- every *_in_txn in store.rs, all of index.rs's
helpers, labels.rs/props.rs/id.rs, plus the executor's call sites. 1-3 days,
no behavior change, existing tests are the net. Expected: ~5.3s -> ~4.0s
(replay-only, on the recommendations load script).

Verify with the replay-only flamegraph (marsdb/examples/convert_only.rs +
profile_load.rs -- currently untracked scratch, may be worth committing as
real tooling given how directly this whole thread has paid off).

After this + the template-parse hoist (see mars-9wj), the flame should read
mostly create_edge_in_txn/lookup_exact -- i.e. actual B-tree work. That's v1's
honest floor for this workload; further load gains mean sorted-by-key
insertion or the v2 storage engine conversation.

comments.author: knoguchi
comments.text: Correction: the template-parse-hoist issue referenced above is mars-afi (typo'd as mars-9wj in the previous comment).

title: Phase B: percentiles, VariableAlreadyBound check, mars-w37
description: percentileCont/percentileDisc aggregates (Aggregation6, 6 reject). VariableAlreadyBound compile-time check for CREATE/MERGE reusing a node var with new label/prop constraints (Create1[19], Merge5[22], 2 unexp). mars-w37: undirected variable-length hop wrong row count (Match5[27]).

title: ANTLR migration: replace pest Cypher parser
description: Rebuild marsdb-query's Cypher parser against openCypher's grammar via ANTLR4 (rrevenantt Rust fork), replacing cypher.pest. See plan at /Users/knoguchi/.claude/plans/purrfect-leaping-shell.md. On branch 'antlr'. Baseline: TCK 3601/3880.

title: Phase 5: existential subqueries (~9 scenarios)
description:
`WHERE EXISTS { MATCH (n)-[:REL]->(m) WHERE m.x > 5 }` — subquery block used as boolean predicate. Correlated against outer scope.

Current: parser rejects `EXISTS` keyword in this form.

Acceptance: +9 scenarios pass. expressions/existentialSubqueries all green.

title: Phase A: TCK harness fixes (path literals, float edge cases)
description: tck_value.rs: parse path-literal expected cells (<(:A)-[:T]->(:B)> format) and float edge cases (scientific notation, NaN) in expected-result comparison. Fixes ~18-20 unsup scenarios (all 12 Match6 + Literals5's 6), possibly more once path parsing lands (recheck Match7/ReturnOrderBy1/WithOrderBy1).

title: Phase D: EXISTS subqueries and CALL procedures
description: EXISTS { <pattern-or-query> } subqueries (ExistentialSubquery1/2/3, ~14 reject) -- needs new Statement/Expr shape, own design pass. CALL procedures (clauses/call, 36 reject) -- needs real procedure-call grammar/executor path plus marsdb-tck harness support for TCK's inline mock-procedure Gherkin steps. Largest remaining item; mars-82w already tracks CALL as its own epic -- this should defer to/merge with that rather than duplicate.
notes: Simple EXISTS {} form landed (commit 237bd26): ExistentialSubquery1's 4 scenarios now pass. Full form (exists { MATCH ... RETURN ... }, ExistentialSubquery2/3, 5 remaining reject) still needs running an arbitrary correlated nested Statement against the current row -- deliberately deferred, real design work. CALL procedures (36 reject) untouched, still defers to mars-82w.

title: Phase 6: CALL procedures (~36 scenarios)
description:
Parse `CALL proc.name(args) YIELD result_col1, result_col2` and standalone `CALL proc(args)`.

Needs:
1. Grammar for CALL + YIELD (with/without YIELD, with/without RETURN after, YIELD *)
2. Procedure registry — at minimum the procedures TCK exercises. Likely string-manipulation / db-metadata procs. Check Call4/5/6 feature files to enumerate.
3. Wire result schema to downstream clauses

Acceptance: +36 scenarios pass. clauses/call all green.

title: Push TCK conformance toward 100% (from 94.4%)
description:
Epic tracking the phased plan at /Users/knoguchi/.claude/plans/purrfect-leaping-shell.md. Phase A: tck_value.rs harness fixes (path literals, float edge cases). Phase B: percentiles, VariableAlreadyBound check, mars-w37. Phase C: aggregate composition, pattern comprehension, list/node/rel-valued params. Phase D: EXISTS subqueries, CALL procedures (mars-82w).

Explicitly excluded: Temporal10[1] (deliberate invariant tradeoff, declined), Match9 (TCK's own "deprecated scenarios").

title: return_expr_references_var treats every Call as scan-var-dependent, blocking IndexSeek for literal-arg calls (e.g. date("...") from $param substitution)
description:
Found in review of PR #154 (temporal $param support). property_value_to_return_expr
rewrites a temporal-valued param into a call to its own constructor, e.g.
date("2020-06-15") -- a ReturnExpr::Call with only literal args, no free
variables.

But return_expr_references_var (marsdb-query/src/planner.rs:454) conservatively
treats ANY ReturnExpr::Call as "might reference the scan var", defaulting to
"don't promote" for IndexSeek eligibility. So a query like:

  MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.released = $d

or the {released: row.date} shape inside a param-bound relationship-creation
statement, silently falls back to a full label scan per row instead of an
IndexSeek -- the exact perf trap this PR series (group commit + parameterized
loading) has been fighting, one dataset-with-dated-indexed-property away.

Fix: teach return_expr_references_var that a Call whose args are all
provably variable-free (recursively, via the same function) references
nothing either -- makes these row-independent and IndexSeekValue::Fixed-eligible,
without needing the larger Literal-widening change (adding a Literal::Date
variant) that's out of scope for the temporal-param work itself.

Verify with a real EXPLAIN-based test: MATCH (n:Label) WHERE n.indexedProp = $d
(with $d bound as a Date param) should show IndexSeek in the plan, not
NodeByLabelScan + Filter.

title: Re-profile bulk load at 5.25s baseline (post-#153/#154) to rank remaining execution-side costs
description: After #153 (group commit, 69.1s->12.1s) and #154 (parameterized replay, ->5.25s), the old flamegraph (70% ANTLR parse) is stale. Re-run cargo flamegraph --example profile_load on the 9,771-statement recommendations script to rank what's left. Expected suspects: per-batch template parse, index maintenance (indexes_for_labels full INDEX_DEFS scan + resolve_label/resolve_prop string round-trips per node created), per-call open_table, executor row machinery (mars-32d). Rank mars-32d/mars-b54/table-handle-caching by this flame before spending.

comments.author: knoguchi
comments.text:
Re-profiled (cargo flamegraph --example profile_load, replay-only -- split
conversion into a separate convert_only.rs step so the flame isn't buried
under the already-understood ANTLR-parse cost again). 5.28s measured,
matches the 5.25s baseline.

New distribution (78.54% of total time is inside execute_in_write_transaction):
- 23.67% redb WriteTransaction::open_table (summed across ~26 monomorphized
  call sites) -- opening tables fresh on every *_in_txn call instead of once
  per transaction. Confirms the design review's "statement-scoped table-handle
  cache" prediction, now with a real number.
- 18.05% create_edge_in_txn (16,648 MATCH+MATCH+CREATE relationship statements)
- 9.96% index::lookup_exact (index seeks feeding those MATCH clauses)
- 7.38% parse_antlr (residual per-statement *template* parse -- small now that
  templates are tiny, this is the expected leftover from #154)
- 4.37% create_node_in_txn
- ~2.9% index::on_node_created (index maintenance)
- 2.56% substitute_params

mars-32d's target (HashMap<String,Binding> row machinery / BindingRow clones)
does NOT appear anywhere in this flame -- zero visible frames. Makes sense:
this workload is bulk CREATE/single-hop MATCH, not multi-hop traversal reads,
so there's no row-clone-per-emitted-neighbor cost to show up. This flame does
NOT rank mars-32d as the top lever for THIS workload -- table-handle caching
(23.67%, no open beads issue yet) and index::lookup_exact/on_node_created
(~13%, also no issue yet) rank higher here. mars-32d's real case is read-side
multi-hop MATCH, not bulk load -- worth a read-path flamegraph (LDBC-shaped
query, not this load script) before ranking it against these, rather than
assuming write-path findings carry over.

title: Label-first AdjEntry key order: typed expansion as prefix range (format bump, bundle with other v2 format breaks)
description: Design review finding: AdjEntry::encode = edge_id++other++label_id, so a node's multimap entries sort by edge id and a typed expansion (-[:KNOWS]->) decodes+label-checks every entry: O(total degree). Reorder to label_id++edge_id++other and typed hops become a redb prefix range: O(matching degree). Matters most on high-degree nodes with many rel types. Costs: on-disk format bump (CURRENT_FORMAT_VERSION), MultimapTableHandle needs a range method (currently get/iter only, deliberately). Bundle with any other format-breaking v2 decisions (e.g. interned prop-name keys in NodeRecord) so the format breaks once.

title: Loader re-parses the statement template once per group instead of once per unique text
description:
Found in mars-9ja's re-profile (see comment): residual per-statement template
parse is 7.38% of replay time, substitute_params another 2.56% -- ~10% combined,
on the real 9,771-statement recommendations load.

The replay loop (marsdb/examples/profile_load.rs, and the shape any real
parameterized loader should follow) currently re-parses each statement's
Cypher TEXT from scratch every time, even when the same template text repeats
across many rows/groups (e.g. every "UNWIND $rows AS row CREATE (n:Person
{tmdbId: row.tmdbId}) SET n += row.properties SET n:Actor" statement in the
dump is byte-identical text, just with a different $rows param each time).

Fix: parse once per *unique* statement text, keep the parsed Statement AST
around, and substitute_params into a *clone* of the pristine AST per group
instead of re-parsing text each time. Loader-side change only (doesn't touch
marsdb-query's public API) -- Statement needs Clone (check), and the loader
needs a HashMap<String template, Statement> cache keyed by the rewritten
template text.

Cheap, mechanical, no engine change. Worth folding into mars-3va's
before/after measurement run (same flamegraph), or as its own ~20-line PR
first since it's independent and lower-risk.

Expected: kills most of both the 7.38% parse tower and the 2.56%
substitute_params tower (the substitute step itself is real work per
group, but the redundant re-parse it currently follows isn't).

comments.author: knoguchi
comments.text:
Implemented in marsdb/examples/profile_load.rs (scratch, untracked):
HashMap<&str, Statement> cache keyed by template text, parse once per
unique text, clone + substitute_params per use instead of re-parsing.

Before/after, real (unprofiled) run:
- Before: 5.28s (matches the 5.25s baseline)
- After: 4.89s (~7.4% faster)

Flamegraph confirms the mechanism, not just the wall-clock: parse_antlr
doesn't appear anywhere in the top-level frame listing anymore (was 7.38%
before). substitute_params is ~flat in absolute time (3.23% of a smaller
total ~= 2.56% of the old total) -- expected, that work didn't change,
only its relative share did.

open_table sum unchanged: 23.21% (was 23.67%) -- confirms mars-3va is a
fully separate, still-fully-available lever, not double-counted with this
fix.

Correctness verified: replayed DB has correct node count (28,863) and
correct property values (dates, names) via a spot-check query.

title: Expose redb Durability::Eventual as opt-in load-mode knob
description: redb commit = CoW page writes + fsync + root flip; Durability::Eventual defers the fsync (crash loses recent commits, never consistency — same class as synchronous_commit=off). Stacks with execute_batch_grouped for load workloads. Expose as opt-in open-mode or per-Database knob; document the crash window. Trivial diff; decide API surface (open builder vs ExecutionOptions is the only real question).

title: Phase 4: ANTLR migration cleanup/docs
description: Document two-stage regen procedure (XML->G4 via openCypher Maven tool, G4->Rust via pinned fork jar) in marsdb-query/grammar/README.md. Update marsdb-tck/VENDOR.md and CYPHER_COVERAGE.md.

title: execute_batch_grouped_with_options: observer/cancellation/timeout for long bulk loads
description: From PR #153 review: execute_batch_grouped (marsdb/src/lib.rs) has no ExecutionOptions path — no observer, cancellation, or timeout. It exists specifically for long bulk loads, the exact case wanting all three; an hours-long load is currently uncancellable and invisible to the observer. Parity gap shared with execute_batch. Add execute_batch_grouped_with_options; thread guard through executor.execute_in_write_transaction_with_options.

title: Phase 1: quick-win grammar fixes (~30 scenarios)
description:
Small, high-ROI grammar/semantic fixes. Target: chained comparisons in WHERE (`WHERE 1 < x < 3`), temporal null propagation (`date(null)`), temporal `.transaction`/`.statement`/`.realtime` variants, other small gaps surfaced by TCK.

Acceptance: +30 scenarios pass in TCK.

Source: /tmp/tck-rejects.log categorization.

title: Phase 3: Cutover to ANTLR parser
description: Point lib.rs parse/parse_many at new implementation. Delete cypher.pest + ~90% of parser.rs. Remove pest/pest_derive deps. Hard gate: full TCK >= 3601/3880, full smoke.rs+ldbc_is_queries.rs+planner.rs, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Phase 7: TCK runner fixture support (~43 unsup)
description:
MarsDB can run these queries but TCK runner can't parse expected-output fixtures. Fix runner:
- Named-path fixed-length output format (11) — path string representation
- Float literal very-long forms `.1e+308` (6) — parser doesn't accept
- Param-based list/map dynamic access `list[$p]` (10) — runner step parser doesn't handle
- `RETURN *` (1) — runner step parser
- Path variable forwarding (2)
- `UNWIND $param` (2) — list-valued parameter
- `null IN [...]` (1)
- Distinct-type ordering output (4)
- `keys($map)` (1)
- Other small (6)

Acceptance: +43 scenarios pass. All `RunnerUnsupported` drops to 0.

title: Phase 2: aggregate nested in expression (~25 scenarios)
description:
Allow aggregates inside wrapping arithmetic/function expressions. Real Cypher accepts `RETURN count(x) + 1`, `RETURN avg(a.age) * 2`, `RETURN max(a.age) + min(a.age)`. Currently MarsDB rejects "aggregate function must be a return item's entire expression".

Fix executor: compute aggregate first over group, then apply outer arithmetic using the grouped-then-aggregated values.

Acceptance: +25 scenarios pass. Return6, With6, ReturnOrderBy2, List12, Delete5 related tests green.

title: TCK: Fix 1000 failing conformance cases
description: TCK shows 2890/3880 passing — ~1000 failing. Need to find what's failing and fix or implement them.

title: Phase 4: pattern comprehension (~11 scenarios)
description:
New expression syntax: `[ pattern | projection ]` where pattern is a graph pattern like `(n)-->()`. Correlated against outer scope, projects one row per match into a list.

Example: `RETURN [p = (n)-->() | p] AS list` for each `n` matched earlier.

Acceptance: +11 scenarios pass. Pattern2.feature all green.

title: Phase 2: ANTLR visitor/AST builder, clause by clause
description: New marsdb-query/src/antlr_visitor.rs, built incrementally per clause (literals->patterns->MATCH->RETURN/WITH->WHERE/expr->mutating clauses->UNION/CALL). Re-derive ~200-250 lines of embedded semantic logic from parser.rs per clause. Resolve ~15+ pest ordered-choice/lookahead spots against ANTLR ALL(*). Parallel parse_antlr() entry point, not wired into lib.rs yet.
notes:
Phase 3 gate cleared. Ran a full behavioral dry-run (temporarily pointed lib.rs parse/parse_many at parse_antlr/parse_antlr_many, ran full test suite + full TCK, reverted after): smoke.rs 349/349, ldbc_is_queries.rs 7/7, full TCK EXECUTION 3633/3880 -- exceeds pest's own 3601/3880 baseline. This is the real Phase 3 hard-gate metric (not just parse-parity).

Found and fixed via the dry-run (9 issues total): precedence bug (IN/STARTS WITH/IS NULL bound tighter than arithmetic -- real vendored-grammar defect, verified against openCypher.bnf, sent upstream), bare CREATE statement shape (explain.rs depends on Statement::Create vs Match{tail} distinction), hex literal suffix-detection bug, list-comprehension/list-literal ambiguity (real bug, sent upstream), a real panic in multiPartQ's trailing-CREATE handling, plus 3 "wrong pest impl not real Cypher" cases fixed at the test level per explicit user direction (exists() as bare function, chained unary minus, UNWIND's own WHERE -- none in openCypher.bnf/TCK) and 1 cosmetic error-message wording difference.

2 more commits added to the draft upstream grammars-v4 PR (precedence fix, list-comprehension ambiguity fix) -- user needs to push (same SSH access limit as before).

lib.rs currently still points at parser::{parse, parse_many} (pest) -- the dry-run swap was reverted each time. The actual Phase 3 cutover (make the swap permanent, delete cypher.pest + ~90% of parser.rs, remove pest deps) has NOT been done -- that's mars-cuk's job, a separate, larger, more destructive step needing explicit user go-ahead.

title: create_edge_in_txn's endpoint-existence checks may be provably redundant after a same-statement IndexSeek
description:
Noted during mars-3va's review, explicitly NOT to act on yet -- backlog/
watch item, not a queued fix.

create_edge_in_txn does two nodes.get() calls (src/dst existence checks)
per edge created. With a write-context table-handle cache in hand (mars-3va)
these get cheaper, but there's a deeper potential win: when src/dst just
came out of an IndexSeek earlier in the SAME statement (the common
relationship-creation shape: MATCH (a:X {indexed}) MATCH (b:Y {indexed})
CREATE (a)-[:REL]->(b)), the existence check is provably redundant -- the
index seek already confirmed the node exists in this transaction's view.

Don't implement this now: correctness-sensitive (needs a real plan-level
proof that the binding truly came from a same-txn lookup with no
intervening delete, not just "looks like it probably did"), out of scope
for the mechanical mars-3va refactor.

File/prioritize only if create_edge_in_txn still tops the flame after
mars-3va + mars-afi land -- check via the same replay-only flamegraph
(marsdb/examples/profile_load.rs) before spending design time on this.

title: VarExpand edge-isomorphism doesn't exclude a var-length hop's own edges from later hops
description:
LogicalPlan::VarExpand's exclude_edge_vars only seeds a variable-length hop's BFS with edges bound by EARLIER fixed hops of the same pattern -- the reverse direction (a variable-length hop's own internally-traversed edges being excluded by a LATER hop in the same pattern) isn't tracked at all. This causes a real double-count bug for patterns mixing a variable-length hop with another hop that reuses a relationship variable.

Found via TCK's Match4 [7]: `MATCH ()-[r:EDGE]-() MATCH p = (n)-[*0..1]-()-[r]-()-[*0..1]-(m) RETURN count(p) AS c` expects 32, got 52 -- confirmed via a full TCK run after briefly lifting parse_helpers.rs's validate_named_path_pattern restriction (which exists specifically to keep this gap unreachable for named-path capture). Reverted that lift (see commit 03b7fa7) rather than shipping the wrong result.

Also blocks TCK's Match6 [14]/[17] and Match7 [19] (named-path capture mixing a variable-length hop with another hop) -- those 3 scenarios don't happen to trigger the double-count themselves, but validate_named_path_pattern can't tell the difference between a pattern that would and one that wouldn't, so all mixing stays rejected together.

Real fix needs VarExpand's own BFS to also track its own traversed edges going forward into later hops' exclude_edge_vars (not just seed from earlier ones) -- likely means a per-row/per-candidate edge set needs to survive past the VarExpand stage into whatever hop comes next, not just get folded into an isomorphism check that only happens today for the *next hop's own* exclude_edge_vars, seeded once at plan-build time (planner.rs's prior_rel_vars), not per-row.

title: Phase 3: var-length path features (~34 scenarios)
description:
Two related features:
1. Bind variable to var-length rel `[r:TYPE*1..3]` — currently rejected as "binding a variable name to a variable-length relationship isn't supported". Should collect the list of relationships.
2. Named-path capture over var-length `p = (a)-[*]->(b)` — currently rejected as "named-path capture over a variable-length relationship pattern isn't supported". Should construct path value with nodes+rels in order.

Acceptance: +34 scenarios pass. Match4, Match6, Match7, Match9, Path2, Path3, Quantifier related tests green.

title: Wrong results for undirected multi-hop patterns with repeated end node
description:
TCK Match6[12] "Matching path with multiple bidirectional relationships" and Match5[27] "Handling mixed relationship patterns and directions 2" return wrong row counts (not errors) -- e.g. `MATCH p=(n)<-->(k)<-->(n) RETURN p` expects 4 rows, gets 2.

Not a regression from the ANTLR migration: pest's own TCK baseline (CYPHER_COVERAGE.md) shows wrong=0 for clauses/match -- pest's grammar apparently couldn't parse this `<-->`-shaped undirected-pattern-with-repeated-node shape at all (counted as reject). ANTLR's grammar parses it fine, newly exposing a latent executor.rs bug in path enumeration / edge-isomorphism handling for undirected multi-hop patterns where the end node repeats an earlier one.

Root cause not yet investigated -- likely in build_match_plan's Expand/edge-isomorphism logic (executor.rs) for the RelDirection::Either case combined with the "bound-node repetition" handling.
notes:
Partially fixed. Root cause found: build_relationship_pattern (antlr_visitor.rs) resolved a relationship pattern with BOTH arrowheads present (`<-[...]->`) as RelDirection::Left instead of RelDirection::Either (an `if LT ... else if GT ...` chain checked LT first, silently ignoring a simultaneously-present GT). Fixed to match on (LT present, GT present) properly: both-or-neither -> Either.

This fixed Match6[12] (now passes) and Create2[20]/Merge5-adjacent CREATE-with-both-arrows cases (now correctly hit the existing "CREATE/MERGE requires a directed relationship" check instead of silently succeeding with the wrong direction).

Still open: Match5[27] "Handling mixed relationship patterns and directions 2" -- still wrong result (expected 16 rows, got 0). Different shape: `<-[:LIKES*3]->` (undirected + variable-length hop combined). Likely a separate executor bug in variable-length traversal not correctly handling RelDirection::Either together with hop_range. Not yet investigated.

title: Phase C: aggregate composition, pattern comprehension, param widening
description: RETURN 1 + count(x) (Return6/With6, ~14 reject) -- generalize per-group evaluator beyond detect-and-reject. Pattern comprehension [(n)-->()|expr] (Pattern2, 11 reject). List/node/rel-valued query parameters (~20 unsup, needs PropertyValue/Value param-path widening in marsdb/marsdb-graph).

title: Named-path capture over a variable-length hop (MATCH p = (a)-[*..N]->(b))
description:
TCK: Quantifier1/2/3/4's [8]/[9] (8 reject) + ReturnOrderBy2 [12] (1 reject) -- all rejected with "named-path capture over a variable-length relationship pattern isn't supported yet". Also would fix Pattern2 [9] (pattern comprehension's own variable-length path capture, same underlying gap).

Root cause: assemble_path/name_pattern_for_path (executor.rs) walk pattern.hops expecting one (rel,node) token per hop with a single bound node/edge id each -- doesn't generalize to a variable-length hop, which represents a variable number of intermediate nodes/edges. expand_variable_row's BFS only tracks (final NodeId, used-edges HashSet) per candidate, not the ordered intermediate path.

Real fix needs the full ordered path (ordered Vec<EdgeId> alongside the existing HashSet, or equivalent) threaded through: VarExpandSpec/expand_variable_row (to build+bind the path), LogicalPlan::VarExpand (a new path_var field), and build_match_plan (to know when to set it -- currently doesn't receive path_var at all, that's handled by execute_match's own post-processing today). validate_named_path_pattern currently rejects this outright; needs relaxing for the single-hop, hop_range-present case specifically (leave multi-hop mixed fixed+variable path capture rejected, not tested by TCK).

Deliberately deferred this session (mars-858) -- contained but genuinely bigger than the other Phase D-adjacent fixes, touches the planner/IR, not just executor.rs.
